backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, with probability 0.3 pick a circle that has fewer than 3 contacts (gap < 1e-6 to other circles or walls, a rattler) instead of the smallest circle, and reinsert it at a random position with radius 0. Otherwise keep the smallest-circle rule. Compute contacts with a vectorised distance matrix. Accept only improvements, as now.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation move

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, pass bounds to SLSQP: each centre may move at most 0.1 from its current value, and radii are in [0, 0.5]. The reinserted circle gets full bounds [0,1]. The smaller feasible box makes each solve converge faster and so gives more reinsertion steps in the same budget. Implement by adding an optional bounds argument to _optimise.
backlog.title: Move-limited SLSQP after reinsertion

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, on every second step use a split move instead of a uniform random reinsertion. Take the smallest circle i (as now) and the circle j chosen uniformly among the 5 largest. Draw a random angle theta; set the centre of j to c_j + 0.5*r_j*(cos theta, sin theta) and the centre of i to c_j - 0.5*r_j*(cos theta, sin theta), with both radii set to 0.45*r_j. Then run _optimise from this point, clip, repair and accept if the sum improves, exactly as for the other steps. This redistributes area from an oversized circle into the removed one, a topology change that a random reinsertion at radius 0 rarely achieves.
backlog.title: Split-the-largest move alternating with reinsertion

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after drawing the uniform random centres, set each initial radius to half of the distance to its nearest other centre, further capped at the distance to the nearest wall and at 0.2. Use these radii as the SLSQP starting point in place of the constant INIT_RADIUS. Leave the restart logic and repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Tangent-distance initial radii from nearest neighbours

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, choose the circle to remove at random with probability proportional to 1/(r_i+0.01)^2 instead of always the smallest, so that the 2nd and 3rd smallest circles are also tried. Reinsert at a random uniform position with radius 0. Everything else stays as is.
backlog.title: Adaptive removal choice by radius weights

backlog.spec: After the restart phase, keep the two best distinct restart packings (sums that differ by more than 1e-4). Run the remove-and-reinsert loop on both in alternation, one step each per iteration, until half of the remaining budget is used. Then drop the weaker chain and spend the rest of the budget on the stronger one. Return the best repaired packing seen. If only one distinct packing exists, use the current behaviour. This hedges against committing early to a poor basin, and it is simpler than full round-robin over many elites.
backlog.title: Two independent reinsertion chains with the time split

backlog.spec: Make two changes to the incumbent. (1) In _optimise, give SLSQP an analytic objective gradient (jac = 0 for the centres, -1 for the radii) and an analytic constraint Jacobian. For the pair rows, use d/dc_i = (c_i-c_j)/dist, d/dc_j = -that, and -1 for r_i and r_j. Use a floor of 1e-12 on dist. The wall rows and the r>=0 rows are fixed ±1 entries. Build the Jacobian as a dense (m, 3n) array, with the index arrays computed once per call. (2) In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a candidate whose sum is lower with probability exp((s2 - s)/T). T starts at 0.003 and falls linearly to 0 by the end of the budget. Draw the probability from rng. Always keep a separate best-ever (c, r) and return it. Every returned packing still goes through _repair.
backlog.title: Combine analytic Jacobians with annealed acceptance

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion phase, build the elite packing, then insert one extra circle at the largest hole (best of 300 random points by distance to the nearest circle edge) with radius 0. Run SLSQP on n+1 circles. Delete the smallest circle and run SLSQP on the remaining n circles to re-expand the others. Accept if the repaired sum improves. Make _optimise accept any circle count.
backlog.title: Solve n+1 then delete the smallest

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop of solve, replace the choice i = np.argmin(r2) with a uniformly random index i = rng.integers(n) so that any circle, not only the smallest, is removed and reinserted each step. Keep the same reinsertion (uniform random centre, r = 0), the same _optimise call, the same _repair, and the same accept-if-better rule. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Random-victim removal in the reinsertion loop

backlog.spec: Combine the two replicated near-winners. In _solve_once, build the initial centres as a Latin hypercube sample in [0.1, 0.9]^2. For each axis, take rng.permutation(n), add rng.uniform(0, 1, n), divide by n, then map to [0.1, 0.9]. In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a worse candidate with probability exp((s2 - s)/T), with T falling linearly from 0.003 to 0 over the reinsertion phase. Track the best-ever repaired packing separately and return it. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: LHS starts plus annealed reinsertion acceptance

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, choose the new centre of the removed circle as follows. With probability 1/3, use a random corner offset by uniform(0.01, 0.08) on each axis toward the inside. With probability 1/3, use a random wall position: one coordinate is uniform(0.02, 0.98) and the other is uniform(0.01, 0.06) from a randomly chosen wall. Otherwise use a uniform point, as now. Use rng for every draw. Small circles in the best packings often sit in corner and wall gaps, which uniform sampling rarely hits.
backlog.title: Corner and wall-biased reinsertion sites

backlog.spec: In _repair, when the most-overlapping pair (i, j) is found, shrink only the larger of the two radii by the full overlap amount, instead of scaling both radii by the ratio d / (r_i + r_j). Clamp the result at zero. Keep the loop count of 50 and the final SHRINK subtraction. This keeps the smaller circle intact and may preserve more total radius.
backlog.title: Single-radius shrink repair

backlog.spec: Add a helper _optimise_local(n, c, r, idx) that runs SLSQP only over the centres and radii of the circles in idx (the reinserted circle plus its 8 nearest circles by centre distance to the new position), with all other circles held fixed. Constraints: pair non-overlap among the free circles, non-overlap of each free circle with each fixed circle, walls and r>=0 for the free circles; objective is minus the sum of free radii; maxiter 100. In the reinsertion loop, use this local solve for each step (it has 27 variables instead of 78, so it is several times faster), repair the result, and accept if the total sum improves. After every accepted step, and in any case every 20 steps, run the existing full _optimise on the current packing to let the improvement propagate, with the usual repair and accept-if-better check.
backlog.title: Local-subproblem SLSQP for each reinsertion

backlog.spec: Pass a separate iteration cap to _optimise. During the random-restart phase use MAX_ITER_RESTART = 60 so that many starts fit into the budget, and during the reinsertion loop use MAX_ITER_POLISH = 400 so that each polish converges. Add an argument maxiter to _optimise and forward it to the minimize options. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Phase-dependent SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, accept a candidate if its sum is at least the current sum minus a threshold that decays linearly from 0.004 to 0 over the loop's time. Keep a separate record of the best packing seen and return it at the end. This is deterministic threshold accepting and differs from the Metropolis rule already tried, because it uses a time-decaying cap and has no probability.
backlog.title: Threshold accepting in reinsertion

backlog.spec: Add a second move to the remove-and-reinsert loop, used with probability 0.5. Pick a random circle j among the 10 largest. Set r[j] to 0.6*r[j]. Set the smallest circle's centre to c[j] plus a random offset of length 0.7*r_old[j], and its radius to 0. Re-optimise with _optimise from this start, then clip, repair, and accept if the sum improves (as the existing move does). The other half of the time, do the existing random reinsertion. This opens space inside dense regions, which uniform reinsertion cannot do.
backlog.title: Shrink-a-neighbour radius transfer move

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, do not always remove argmin(r). Sort the circles by radius and pick one of the 6 smallest at random, with probability proportional to 1/(rank+1). Use rng for the draw. Then do what the code does now: set its centre uniformly at random, set its radius to 0, re-solve, repair, and accept only if the sum improves. The aim is to stop the loop from failing on the same circle over and over once the smallest circle is already well placed.
backlog.title: Rank-weighted choice of the circle to remove

backlog.spec: Give _optimise an optional maxiter argument defaulting to MAX_ITER. In the remove-and-reinsert loop call it with maxiter=50, since the warm start is near a local optimum and most steps fail; this gives about three to four times more reinsertion attempts. End the loop at 0.9 of the budget rather than at the full budget, then run one final _optimise on the best packing with maxiter=400, clip and repair it, and keep it only if its repaired sum of radii is larger than the unpolished one. The random-restart phase keeps MAX_ITER = 200.
backlog.title: Short SLSQP solves in the reinsertion loop, full polish at the end

backlog.spec: After each _optimise call (and before _repair), fix the centres and solve the radius-only problem as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance of centre i, r_i >= 0. Use the LP radii in place of SLSQP radii if they are valid and larger. This removes the slack left by SLSQP's loose tolerance and gives exactly tight radii, so _repair rarely has to shrink anything. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius polish after SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the final best packing is chosen, identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT-style system by running a second SLSQP call from the best point with tight ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=500, using only the constraints for near-active pairs (gap < 0.05) plus all wall constraints. Accept the result only if it is valid after _repair and has a larger sum. Use the last 5 percent of the time budget for this.
backlog.title: Active-contact Newton polish

memo: Helped: slot 0 (remove-smallest-and-reinsert after a short random-restart phase) is the incumbent at -2.6311 (runs -2.6305, -2.6316; delta -0.0031). Several replicated variants sit near or below the incumbent but were rejected: slot 18 annealing acceptance (-2.6348/-2.6332), slot 4 Latin hypercube starts (-2.6343/-2.6335), slot 30 hex/uniform alternation (-2.6337/-2.6317), slot 34 multi-removal (-2.6334/-2.6313). Their deltas are within noise of slot 0 and may be worse or equal. Slot 32 analytic gradients (-2.6330, one run) and slot 7 log-normal radii (-2.6325, one run) are unreliable at noise sd 0.0023. Did not help: basin hopping (+0.0030), position screening (+0.0023), sparse constraints (+0.0021), ring starts (+0.0037), mirror starts (+0.0036), squeeze (+0.0015); most other tweaks about +-0.0002. Next: combine slot 0 with LHS starts, the slot 18 acceptance rule and analytic gradients (faster SLSQP), replicate at least twice, then add the slot 7 radii init. Avoid single-run conclusions.
